pages.ja:
なにやら思案げな風で、人の弁当をつつく遠坂。
遠坂は今日も手ぶらで屋上に来ていた。
つまり昼飯の用意などしていなかったのだ。
となると、唯一の食料である俺の弁当が狙われるのも、これまた必然と言えた。

pages.en:
Tohsaka looks deep in thought as she picks at someone else’s lunch.

She came to the roof empty-handed again today.

In other words, she had made no provision whatsoever for lunch.

That being the case, it was perhaps inevitable that she would set her sights upon my bento, the only food available.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka ponders as she eats my lunch.
She came to the rooftop empty-handed.
Which, of course, meant that she didn’t have her lunch.
Then it was only natural for her to target mine.

pages.ja: 「いいから食べろ。……ったく、弁当持ってないクセにさ、どうして箸だけは完備してんだよ。おまえ、箸いつも持ち歩いてんのか？」

pages.en: “Enough talk. Just eat. …Honestly, how is it that you don’t have a bento, but you’re fully equipped with chopsticks? Do you carry them around all the time?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Just eat. …Man, why do you have chopsticks when you don’t have your own lunch? Do you always carry them around?”

pages.ja: 「？ これは教室出る時にもってきただけよ？ 衛宮くん、この前もお昼ご飯持ってたから、今日も分けてもらえばいいかなって。で、もしお弁当だった時を考えて、事前に箸を用意したんだけど？」
pages.jaRuby: 「？ これは教室出る時にもってきただけよ？ 衛宮くん、この前もお昼ご飯持ってたから、今日も分けてもらえばいいかなって。で、もしお弁当だった時を考えて、事前に箸を用意したんだけど？」
pages.en: “Hm? I only brought these when I left the classroom. You had lunch with you the other day, Emiya, so I thought I could ask you to share again. And in case it turned out to be a bento, I prepared the chopsticks in advance. Why?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…? I just brought these with me when I left my classroom. You had your lunch last time, so I thought I’d have you share some of yours. I came prepared just in case you had boxed lunch.”

“…Hey now. I think you’re putting thought into the wrong areas.”

pages.en:
“Liar. You’re the sort who never holds back at a barbecue. I can see it now. Absolutely, positively see it. While I sit there nibbling away at salted squid, you’ll devour marbled short rib as though they were those endless little bowls of soba.

“You’ll eat so much, so fast, with so little regard for the contents of my wallet, that I’ll know you’re deliberately trying to bankrupt me. And after you’ve finally had your fill, you’ll lean back and say, ‘Hmph. I went easy on you this time.’”

Hmph. I deliver the little jab as revenge for earlier, determined to have the last word.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Liar. I bet you’re the type that doesn’t hold back when you go eat yakiniku. I’m suuuuuure of it. You’ll be scarfing down beef ribs while I’ll be munching on my salted fish.
You won’t show any consideration for my money. In fact, you’ll try to bankrupt me. And after you’re satisfied, you’re going to tell me, ‘Heh, I went easy this time.’“
I try to get back at her for what she said earlier.
